project.name: RefundLedger demonstration
project.description: Fictional local authorization ledger; no money movement, payment provider or deployment integration.

uses.rationale: Tenant isolation relies on the principal the identity adapter marks verified.
The ledger's principal is the adapter's verified principal.

environments.title: One reservation attempt observed before and after
One cancel or commit command observed before and after
One audited operation and the audit rows it added
One remaining-capacity request by a verified principal of the ledger tenant, and its answer

nodes.title: Preserve captured capacity

data.description: Prevent local refund authorizations from consuming more than the captured amount.
data.success_measure: Every accepted transition preserves CON-001; concurrency tests include atomic reservation.

nodes.title: Preserve tenant isolation

data.description: Only an authenticated principal for the tenant may operate on that tenant ledger.
data.success_measure: Cross-tenant requests are denied and create no state change.

nodes.title: Minor unit

data.definition: A non-negative integer number of EUR cents. This example has one currency per payment and no conversion.

nodes.title: Captured capacity

data.definition: The immutable captured amount for one tenant/payment pair. This is a local authorization ceiling, not a payment-provider balance.

nodes.title: Consuming reservation

data.definition: A refund record in reserved or committed state; released and rejected records do not consume capacity.

nodes.title: Idempotency scope

data.definition: The tuple tenant_id, payment_id, key. Records are retained for the lifetime of this demonstration ledger.

nodes.title: Verified principal

data.definition: A principal established outside request payloads by a trusted authentication adapter. Test fixtures simulate this adapter.

nodes.title: Reject excess reservation

data.trigger: a reservation would consume more than the captured capacity
data.subject: RefundLedger
data.response: reject the reservation without changing the ledger

nodes.title: Reuse identical request

data.trigger: a request repeats an existing tenant/payment/key with the same payload
data.subject: RefundLedger
data.response: return the existing reservation identifier without adding a record

nodes.title: Reject conflicting reuse

data.trigger: a tenant/payment/key is reused with a different payload
data.subject: RefundLedger
data.response: reject the conflicting request without changing the original record

nodes.title: Deny cross-tenant access

data.trigger: the principal is unverified or the principal, request and target ledger tenants do not all match
data.subject: RefundLedger
data.response: deny the request without disclosing or changing another tenant ledger

nodes.title: Release failed reservation

data.trigger: a reserved authorization is definitively cancelled before commitment
data.subject: RefundLedger
data.response: release its capacity while retaining its idempotency record

nodes.title: Commit exactly one reserved record

data.trigger: an authorized commit command targets a reserved record
data.subject: RefundLedger
data.response: mark that record committed atomically without consuming capacity a second time

nodes.title: Bounded audit diagnostics

data.subject: RefundLedger
data.response: record the operation identifier and outcome without copying credentials or complete request bodies

nodes.title: Record left by a refused reservation

data.question: Does a refused reservation leave a rejected record in the ledger?
options: No record: the ledger is unchanged
A rejected record that consumes no capacity
data.answer: No record: the ledger is unchanged
data.rationale: REQ-001 already requires an unchanged ledger. The rejected status in the environments and MODEL-001 is then not written by this path; whether to remove it stays visible. This is a fictional reference decision.

nodes.title: Command on a record that is not reserved

data.question: What does a cancel or commit command do when its record is not reserved?
options: Report a repeated command as already done and refuse a contradictory one; neither changes the ledger
data.answer: Report a repeated command as already done and refuse a contradictory one; neither changes the ledger
data.rationale: A cancel or commit retried after a lost response must not look like a failure, and a contradictory command, such as cancelling a committed record, must not move a terminal record. This is a fictional reference decision.

nodes.title: Compatibility of the new predicates with release 1.0.0

data.question: Do CON-009, CON-010 and CON-011 require anything that release 1.0.0 did not?
options: No: they state what REQ-004, REQ-005, REQ-006 and REQ-007 already required
data.answer: No: they state what REQ-004, REQ-005, REQ-006 and REQ-007 already required
data.rationale: CON-010 formalizes the transitions REQ-005 and REQ-006 already described. CON-009 reaches REQ-004 only to say that a denied command changes nothing, which REQ-004 already required. CON-011 fixes the audit record of an attempt to one row holding the identifier, the operation kind and the outcome: REQ-007 already required the identifier and the outcome on record and nothing copied from the request. An implementation that satisfied 1.0.0 is not made non-conforming. This is a fictional reference decision.
